name: Business Logic Testing
description: Testing of web application business logic for flaws that automated scanners cannot detect. Covers workflow and state abuse, multi-step process integrity, race conditions, pricing and quantity manipulation, limit and function-use circumvention, and abuse of intended features, following OWASP WSTG Business Logic Testing (WSTG-BUSL). Access control bypass as such belongs to SWSEC-WEB-AUTHZ.

0.label: None
0.description: No exposure to business logic testing

1.label: Awareness
1.description: Understands what business logic flaws are and why they need manual testing
evidence: Can explain business logic flaws and give examples (negative quantities, skipped workflow steps)
Understands race conditions and time-of-check/time-of-use issues in web applications
Familiar with the WSTG-BUSL test cases

2.label: Guided Practice
evidence: Mapped an application's workflows and documented expected business rules before testing
Tested parameter tampering of prices, quantities and discounts in lab applications
Attempted out-of-order and replayed requests in multi-step processes
Findings reviewed by authorized tester before inclusion in reports

3.label: Independent Practice
3.description: Independently identifies and demonstrates business logic flaws
evidence: Independently identified business logic flaws on 5+ engagements
Demonstrates race conditions using parallel or single-packet request techniques
Articulates business impact of logic flaws in reports in terms the client can act on
Passed proficiency assessment on business logic testing

4.label: Advanced / Mentor
4.description: Tests complex transactional systems; chains logic flaws
evidence: Tests payment, booking, loyalty or financial transaction flows end to end
Chains multiple low-severity logic flaws into high-impact exploitation paths
Derives test cases from requirements and threat models with the client
Mentors junior testers on business logic analysis

5.label: Expert / Authority
5.description: Authority on business logic security; develops methodology
evidence: Developed the lab's business logic testing methodology and test-case catalogue
Published research on novel logic or race-condition attack techniques
Advises on secure workflow design for high-value transactional systems
Trains teams on advanced business logic testing

assessment_methods.description: Identify and exploit seeded logic flaws in a prepared e-commerce application, including price manipulation, workflow bypass and a race condition
Given a multi-step business process specification, derive abuse cases and a test plan mapped to WSTG-BUSL
